answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a distinct sensor station, such as a tide gauge on a dune above the ocean, streaming unpredictable measurements that must match neighbouring independent stations. A cloned station fails that cross-check, and sites cannot be bought in bulk because each needs separate installation, inspection, and a distinct real address. For every additional fake identity, the attacker must buy and maintain one more station and pay a site fee that doubles per station on the same funding trail, so the tenth fake costs far more than the first, at the nadir of demand.
